subject: Post-call: Quantization trade-offs & next steps
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>

Cc: Nikhil Sharma <nikhil.sharma@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 26 Feb 2026 15:10:00 -0800
Subject: Post-call: Quantization trade-offs & next steps

Hi Sarah / Mike —

Great to meet earlier — thanks for walking us through the FinWave classification workload and the latency targets. Quick recap from our side and proposed next steps so we stay aligned: 

Call recap
- Primary goal: reduce per-request latency to hit 99th percentile < 200ms for short classification prompts (~40–60 tokens), while keeping quality drop <1-2% absolute on your in-house eval.
- Constraints: on-prem GPU fleet (NVIDIA A100 / T4 mix), strict PII handling, and preference to avoid significant retraining.

Recommendations we discussed (high level)
- Model families to evaluate: LLaMA-2-13B (instruction-tuned), Mistral-7B-Instruct, and a smaller Redwood-Instruct-4B for edge/burst modes.
- Quantization options: AWQ for 7B-class models (best throughput/quality balance), GPTQ for larger 13B (slightly better quant stability), and FP8 as an aggressive throughput-first experiment (higher risk for regressions).

Immediate next steps
1) We’ll share the prompt set and an initial trade-off document (attached). Please confirm the representative prompt slices in finwave-prompt-set-v1.jsonl.
2) Redwood to run a focused A/B eval across FP16 / AWQ / GPTQ / FP8 on Mistral-7B and LLaMA-2-13B using your prompt set. We’ll measure: latency (p50/p95/p99), throughput (tokens/s), and your quality metric (accuracy/F1).
3) Follow-up call to review numbers and decide rollout policy (canary -> dedicated reserved pool).

Tentative timeline: we can have initial numbers by Wednesday next week (Mar 4) if you can confirm the prompt set and grant access to the sample dev dataset.

Attachments: finwave-prompt-set-v1.jsonl, redwood-quant-tradeoff.pdf

Thanks —
Marissa

Subject: Re: Post-call: Quantization trade-offs & next steps

Hi Sarah — great, thanks for the dataset offer. We’ll include class-level deltas in the evaluation. Below are the initial, opinionated tradeoffs and the exact test plan we’ll run so you know what to expect.

Short summary of quantization trade-offs (practical guidance)
- AWQ (per-channel asymmetric weight quantization):
  - Best fit for 7B-class models (Mistral-7B-Instruct).
  - Throughput: ~35 tokens/s on A100 (vs FP16 baseline ~12 tokens/s) for typical 40-token prompts in our infra.
  - Quality: approx ~1–2% absolute drop on classification accuracy for these prompt types (class-level deltas typically concentrated on low-frequency labels).
  - Risk: low-to-moderate; stable in most prompt families.
- GPTQ (post-training quantization):
  - Recommended for larger models (LLaMA-2-13B) when you need to preserve quality.
  - Throughput: ~28 tokens/s on A100 in our runs.
  - Quality: ~0.5–1% absolute drop on your eval; usually less class skew than AWQ on 13B.
  - Risk: moderate; quant kernels can be sensitive to sequence length and KV-cache patterns.
- FP8 (mixed-precision FP8 kernels):
  - Highest throughput potential (~45 tokens/s on some GPUs) but currently experimental for some ops/profiles.
  - Quality: observed 3–5% absolute degradation on edge prompt sets in our internal benchmarking (depends heavily on normalization and activation ranges).
  - Risk: higher; recommend only for non-critical low-latency paths or for canary tests.

Planned A/B eval (what we’ll measure)
- Models: Mistral-7B-Instruct (FP16, AWQ), LLaMA-2-13B (FP16, GPTQ, FP8 as an experiment), Redwood-Instruct-4B (FP16, AWQ)
- Metrics: p50/p95/p99 latency, tokens/s throughput, per-class precision/recall, overall accuracy, and cost-per-1M tokens estimate based on your fleet mix.
- Data: finwave-prompt-set-v1.jsonl (sanitized sample you provide) + small holdout (we’ll keep seed & prompts visible for reproducibility).
- Deliverables: A spreadsheet with numbers, a short doc with recommended rollout (canary thresholds + fallback), and example prompts showing regressions.

Benchmarks and artifacts
- Public trade study: https://docs.redwood.ai/benchmarks/quant-tradeoffs-2026
- Shared drive (read-only): https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b-finwave-evals
- SOC2 / security artifacts: I’ve added a link in the drive (SOC2 report stub) and will introduce our security contact once procurement is ready.

We’ll attach the initial tradeoff PDF and the prompt set in case you want to review offline. Targeting initial numbers by Wed (Mar 4).

Thanks —
Marissa

Subject: Internal: FinWave eval run plan (A/B)

Team —

Moving to internal coordination now that Sarah will send the sanitized sample. Please run the A/B eval below against the sample when it arrives. Deliverable due EOD Tue (Mar 4) so we can present on Wed.

Run plan summary
- Workload: FinWave sample prompts (avg 45 tokens) + holdout 10%.
- Variants: Mistral-7B {FP16, AWQ}, LLaMA-2-13B {FP16, GPTQ, FP8}, Redwood-Instruct-4B {FP16, AWQ}
- Hardware: prefer A100-80GB for 13B runs; T4 or A100 for 7B; record GPU type per run.
- Measurements: p50/p95/p99 latency, tokens/s throughput, memory footprint, per-class precision/recall, and a short example set showing any quality regressions.
- Cost calc: approximate cost-per-1M tokens using our infra pricing.

Notes / priorities
1) Prioritize p99 latency for the 40–60 token slice. If we can’t meet p99 < 200ms with AWQ on Mistral-7B, include a recommendation for LLaMA-2-13B+GPTQ or a smaller model at AWQ as fallback.
2) For FP8 runs mark them as "experimental" in the spreadsheet and capture any prompts that spike error rates.

Please drop interim results in the drive folder and ping me on Slack if any run needs debugging. I’ll consolidate and reply to Sarah with the spreadsheet and a short recommendation doc.

Thanks —
Marissa
